2609.17398.title: Enhancing Accessibility of Medical Texts through Large Language Model-Driven Plain Language Adaptation
2609.17398.paper_summary: This paper addresses the challenge of making complex healthcare information more accessible through automated Plain Language Adaptation (PLA). PLA aims to simplify technical medical language, bridging a critical gap between the complexity of healthcare texts and patients' reading comprehension. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs), such as GPT and BART, have opened new possibilities for PLA, especially in zero-shot and few-shot learning contexts where task-specific data is limited. In this work, we leverage the capabilities of LLMs such as GPT-4o-mini, Gemini-1.5-pro, and LLaMA for text simplification. Additionally, we incorporate Mixture-of-Agents (MoA) techniques to enhance adaptability and robustness in PLA tasks. Key contributions include a comparative analysis of prompting strategies, finetuning with QLoRA on different LLMs, and the integration of MoA technique. Our findings demonstrate the effectiveness of LLM-driven PLA, showcasing its potential in making healthcare information more comprehensible while preserving essential content.
2609.17398.paper_summary_zh: 這篇論文針對如何通過自動化的簡易語言適應（PLA）使複雜的醫療資訊更易於獲取的挑戰進行探討。<lb/>PLA旨在簡化技術性醫療語言，彌合醫療文本的複雜性與患者閱讀理解之間的關鍵差距。<lb/>最近在大型語言模型（LLMs）方面的進展，例如GPT和BART，為PLA開啟了新的可能性，特別是在零樣本和少樣本學習的情境中，這些情境下任務特定的數據有限。<lb/>在本研究中，我們利用LLMs的能力，如GPT-4o-mini、Gemini-1.5-pro和LLaMA來進行文本簡化。<lb/>此外，我們還結合了混合代理（MoA）技術，以增強PLA任務的適應性和穩健性。<lb/>主要貢獻包括對提示策略的比較分析、在不同LLMs上使用QLoRA進行微調，以及MoA技術的整合。<lb/>我們的研究結果顯示了LLM驅動的PLA的有效性，展示了其在使醫療資訊更易於理解的同時保持重要內容的潛力。
